requirements.requirement: Export node1:/srv/nfs/shared by NFS and mount it at /mnt/shared on node2.
requirements.summary: Node1 directly reports the active, node2-restricted export and healthy NFS services. Node2 directly reports the NFSv4 mount at /mnt/shared, its persistent fstab entry, and automatic recovery through nfsmount after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provide dataops with UID and GID 4500 on both nodes, and make the shared directory dataops:dataops with mode 2770.
requirements.summary: Both nodes directly report dataops as UID/GID 4500. The server directory and its client-mounted view both report numeric ownership 4500:4500 and mode 2770, including after restarts.

requirements.requirement: Files created from either node retain consistent ownership and permissions across the share.
requirements.summary: Post-restart writes performed as dataops on each node produced files with UID/GID 4500:4500 and mode 660. Both files were then read and inspected successfully from both nodes with identical metadata and contents.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and bidirectional behavior evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is strong: node1 has a healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, changed boot ID, and recovered server/export/data state; node2 has the same complete sequence after the init-service correction, with automatic mount and data recovery. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the final changed boots on both nodes.
limitations: The generic failed-service lifecycle probe was unsupported on Alpine because it checks systemd; task-specific OpenRC service statuses were nevertheless captured directly.
Lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate boot changes and general host state, but task-specific export, mount, metadata, and data recovery observations come from executor commands.

operational_hygiene.summary: The final system state is coherent, with task-required packages, services, identities, export, mount, and expected NFS runtime files. One unnecessary transient mutation occurred when nfsclient was enabled even though it does not mount NFS filesystems; it caused the first node2 restart to return without the mount and was fully reverted when nfsmount was enabled instead. The restart commands also left /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log on both nodes; these are minor retained temporary-file residues. No package damage, conflicting final service configuration, or unrelated broad mutation is evidenced.
